free_tier.stated: No free Code plan and none under USD 20: Pro is USD 50 and Max USD 200, both marked 'sold out'. The page's 'Free Trial' is 'Limited Free Credits', the platform trial: a one-time USD 5 promotional credit after a valid payment method is added, expiring 30 days after activation
free_tier.notes: the trial credit is spent per token at the Free Trial rate limits; the Code plans meter tokens per day

interface_detail: an API key from cloud.cerebras.ai used from any editor or agent that accepts an OpenAI-compatible endpoint; the vendor names Cline, OpenCode and Crush. There is no Cerebras agent, so the headless mode is whichever agent calls the key
tooling: any OpenAI-compatible coding agent or SDK
chaining: a key for Cline, OpenCode, Crush or Aider; the referral programme raises an account's limits to the Code Pro equivalent after 11 referred sign-ups, which is the only route to Code Pro limits while both plans are sold out

limits.value: Pro: up to 24 million tokens per day; Max: up to 120 million tokens per day

Pro 50 requests and 1,000,000 tokens a minute, Max 120 requests and 1,500,000 tokens a minute; requests per second are 10% of requests per minute (FAQ as archived on 2026-04-22; the live FAQ URL answers 404)
Free Trial: 5 requests a minute, 30K uncached tokens a minute, 1M tokens an hour and 1M tokens a day per model, on gpt-oss-120b and qwen-3.8-27b

binding_note: with Pro and Max sold out, the reachable route is the one-time trial at 1M tokens a day per model, which ends when the USD 5 credit is spent or 30 days pass

identity_cost.detail: a cloud.cerebras.ai account and a valid payment method for the trial credit: 'Add a valid payment method to receive a one-time $5 promotional credit'; Code Pro and Max are prepaid monthly subscriptions

reliability_note: both Code plans are marked sold out; the archived FAQ states operation at near 100% utilisation with requests briefly queued at peak, and 429 errors from per-second limits during bursts
confidence_note: prices, sold-out state, daily token allowances, trial terms and the referral threshold are quoted from first-party pages read on 2026-10-30; the per-minute plan limits come from an archived copy of a FAQ that now answers 404. Whether a sold-out plan can be bought at all is shown only after sign-in.
